# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
"""
Repair Romanian text typed with cedilla letters (ş Ş ţ Ţ) so that it uses the
correct comma-below letters (ș Ș ț Ț).

Nothing else in the text is touched: other characters (including Turkish-style
ç/Ç, which legitimately use a cedilla, and any already-correct comma-below
letters) are left exactly as they are.
"""

# Pre-composed cedilla code points -> pre-composed comma-below code points
_PRECOMPOSED = {
    0x015F: "\u0219",  # ş LATIN SMALL LETTER S WITH CEDILLA  -> ș
    0x015E: "\u0218",  # Ş LATIN CAPITAL LETTER S WITH CEDILLA -> Ș
    0x0163: "\u021B",  # ţ LATIN SMALL LETTER T WITH CEDILLA  -> ț
    0x0162: "\u021A",  # Ţ LATIN CAPITAL LETTER T WITH CEDILLA -> Ț
}

# Decomposed sequences: base letter + U+0327 COMBINING CEDILLA
_DECOMPOSED = {
    "s\u0327": "\u0219",
    "S\u0327": "\u0218",
    "t\u0327": "\u021B",
    "T\u0327": "\u021A",
}


def fix_romanian(text: str) -> str:
    """Replace Romanian cedilla letters with their comma-below equivalents."""
    if not text:
        return text

    # Handle the decomposed (base + combining cedilla) form first.
    if "\u0327" in text:
        for seq, repl in _DECOMPOSED.items():
            text = text.replace(seq, repl)

    # Handle the pre-composed form.
    return text.translate(_PRECOMPOSED)

import re
import unicodedata

# Romanian uses S/T with COMMA BELOW (ș U+0219, ț U+021B, Ș U+0218, Ț U+021A).
# Texts very often (wrongly) carry the Turkish-style CEDILLA variants
# (ş U+015F, ţ U+0163, Ş U+015E, Ţ U+0162) or decomposed combining sequences.
_SINGLE_CHAR_FIXES = {
    "\u015E": "\u0218",  # Ş -> Ș
    "\u015F": "\u0219",  # ş -> ș
    "\u0162": "\u021A",  # Ţ -> Ț
    "\u0163": "\u021B",  # ţ -> ț
}

# base letter + combining mark  ->  precomposed Romanian letter
_SEQUENCE_FIXES = {
    "S\u0326": "\u0218", "S\u0327": "\u0218",  # S + comma/cedilla below -> Ș
    "s\u0326": "\u0219", "s\u0327": "\u0219",  # s + comma/cedilla below -> ș
    "T\u0326": "\u021A", "T\u0327": "\u021A",  # T + comma/cedilla below -> Ț
    "t\u0326": "\u021B", "t\u0327": "\u021B",  # t + comma/cedilla below -> ț
    "A\u0306": "\u0102", "a\u0306": "\u0103",  # A/a + breve        -> Ă/ă
    "A\u0302": "\u00C2", "a\u0302": "\u00E2",  # A/a + circumflex   -> Â/â
    "I\u0302": "\u00CE", "i\u0302": "\u00EE",  # I/i + circumflex   -> Î/î
}

_SEQUENCE_RE = re.compile("|".join(re.escape(k) for k in _SEQUENCE_FIXES))
_CHAR_TABLE = str.maketrans(_SINGLE_CHAR_FIXES)


def fix_romanian(text: str) -> str:
    """Normalize Romanian diacritics to standard orthography.

    - s/t with cedilla (ş, ţ, Ş, Ţ) become s/t with comma below (ș, ț, Ș, Ț)
    - decomposed letters (e.g. "s" + U+0326/U+0327, "a" + U+0306, "i" + U+0302)
      are composed into the proper precomposed characters
    Everything else in the text is left untouched.
    """
    if not text:
        return text

    # Compose decomposed base+combining-mark sequences.
    if any(unicodedata.combining(ch) for ch in text):
        text = _SEQUENCE_RE.sub(lambda m: _SEQUENCE_FIXES[m.group(0)], text)

    # Replace cedilla variants with the correct comma-below letters.
    return text.translate(_CHAR_TABLE)
